page.layout: One page of text, verse in short stanzas, with a running head at the top and the page number at the top right; the printer's name and date closing the page below the last stanza. No margin notes, no column.

main_text.p:
Quanto corporibus mens est sublimior ipsis,
Tanto etiam veteri maior Apelle nouus.
main_text.head: III.

p.i:
Nec minium tabulis, nec purpura fulget in istis:
Sincerus tantum candor vbique nitet,
Cui tamen & minium, cui purpura cesserit ipsa:
Tanta illum vestit gratia, tanta Venus.
Ast vnde hæc tanti vis est candoris? ab illo
Vno quo nihil est pectore candidius.

main_text.head: IIII.

p.i:
Hæc cur non varios habeat pictura colores
Queris? Opus suco non habet istud opus.

main_text.head: V.

p.i:
Quorum animos eelsus iamdudum seruat Olympus,
Terra tenebrosis corpora Sarcophagis:
Illorum in terris animos, in lumine vultus,
Ingenio Beζæ cernimus artificis.
Quid tibi, quid tanto artifice pro munere tali
Exoptent grato pectore Christicolæ?
Nempe vt te incolumi multos speEtemus in annos
In terris vultus, optime Beζa, tuos.
Tu vero illustri post fata receptus Olympo
Æternum spectes ipsius ęra Dei.

page.notes: Printed letters in this page are as they stand. Doubtful: "suco" in the Greek-letter-free line IIII reads as printed; "speEtemus" is printed as "speEtemus" (a long-s/ct ligature, read as "spectemus" in the printed text, left as printed). The Greek word after "Beζ" in line V is the printer's Greek letter zeta-like form ζ, copied as seen. The initial of "Quanto" and "Quorum" are plain. The date "MDCD" is read as printed; the last letter may be a worn D. Roman numerals III, IIII, V are headings set apart in the printed page.
